photograph, the background job runs and writes the derived copy — then the
first reader to open the book triggers the same conversion again, and the
second copy is kept next to the first forever.

Make an upload get derived once. After the background work has run, opening
the book page and fetching the picture it links to does no image processing,
and exactly one derived copy is in storage.

What a reader is served does not change — the same picture they get today,
byte for byte.

Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**

```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html

  end
end
```

**Avoid:**

```ruby
def show
```

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "module ActiveStorage::Sluggable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_create :set_slug
  end

  def slug_path
    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.action_text_markdown_upload_path(slug)
  end

  private
    def set_slug
      self.slug = "#{slug_basename}-#{SecureRandom.alphanumeric(6)}.#{slug_extension}"
    end

    def slug_basename
      File.basename(slug_filename, ".*").parameterize
    end

    def slug_extension
      File.extname(slug_filename).delete(".").parameterize
    end

    def slug_filename
      slug.presence || filename.to_s
    end
end

module ActiveStorage::Sluggable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_create :set_slug
  end

  def slug_path
    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.action_text_markdown_upload_path(slug)
  end

  private
    def set_slug
      self.slug = "#{slug_basename}-#{SecureRandom.alphanumeric(6)}.#{slug_extension}"
    end

    def slug_basename
      File.basename(slug_filename, ".*").parameterize
    end

    def slug_extension
      File.extname(slug_filename).delete(".").parameterize
    end

    def slug_filename
      slug.presence || filename.to_s
    end
end

  ActiveStorage::Attachment.include ActiveStorage::Sluggable

# = Active Storage \Attachment
#
# Attachments associate records with blobs. Usually that's a one record-many blobs relationship,
# but it is possible to associate many different records with the same blob. A foreign-key constraint
# on the attachments table prevents blobs from being purged if they’re still attached to any records.

#   User.all.with_attached_avatars
#
#   # preloads blobs and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
class ActiveStorage::Attachment < ActiveStorage::Record
  define_model_callbacks :upload

  after_upload :mirror_blob_later
  after_upload :analyze_blob_later
  after_upload :create_variants

  # Set to true when immediate variants have been processed from local io,
  # so create_variants knows to skip them.
  attr_accessor :immediate_variants_processed

  # Set to true for fresh uploads (io provided), false for existing blobs.
  # Used to determine whether to run :upload callbacks in after_create_commit.
  attr_accessor :pending_upload

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated record.
  belongs_to :record, polymorphic: true, touch: ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated ActiveStorage::Blob.
  belongs_to :blob, class_name: "ActiveStorage::Blob", autosave: true, inverse_of: :attachments

  delegate_missing_to :blob
  delegate :signed_id, to: :blob

  after_create_commit :run_upload_callbacks, unless: :pending_upload
  after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later

    blob.local_io = io

    process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
    analyze_blob_from_io(io)

    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)

    # Stream the blob in byte ranges specified through the header
    def send_blob_byte_range_data(blob, range_header, disposition: nil)
      ranges = Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(range_header, blob.byte_size)

      return head(:range_not_satisfiable) if ranges.blank? || ranges.all?(&:blank?)

      if ranges.length == 1
        range = ranges.first
        content_type = blob.content_type_for_serving
        data = blob.download_chunk(range)

        response.headers["Content-Range"] = "bytes #{range.begin}-#{range.end}/#{blob.byte_size}"
      else
        boundary = SecureRandom.hex
        content_type = "multipart/byteranges; boundary=#{boundary}"
        data = +""

        ranges.compact.each do |range|
          chunk = blob.download_chunk(range)

          data << "\r\n--#{boundary}\r\n"
          data << "Content-Type: #{blob.content_type_for_serving}\r\n"
          data << "Content-Range: bytes #{range.begin}-#{range.end}/#{blob.byte_size}\r\n\r\n"
          data << chunk
        end

        data << "\r\n--#{boundary}--\r\n"
      end

      response.headers["Accept-Ranges"] = "bytes"
      response.headers["Content-Length"] = data.length.to_s

        filename: blob.filename.sanitized,
        status: :partial_content,
        type: content_type

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "securerandom"

module ActiveStorage::Streaming
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  DEFAULT_BLOB_STREAMING_DISPOSITION = "inline"

  include ActionController::DataStreaming
  include ActionController::Live

  private
    # Stream the blob in byte ranges specified through the header
    def send_blob_byte_range_data(blob, range_header, disposition: nil)
      ranges = Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(range_header, blob.byte_size)

      return head(:range_not_satisfiable) if ranges.blank? || ranges.all?(&:blank?)

      if ranges.length == 1
        range = ranges.first
        content_type = blob.content_type_for_serving
        data = blob.download_chunk(range)

        response.headers["Content-Range"] = "bytes #{range.begin}-#{range.end}/#{blob.byte_size}"
      else
        boundary = SecureRandom.hex
        content_type = "multipart/byteranges; boundary=#{boundary}"
        data = +""

        ranges.compact.each do |range|
          chunk = blob.download_chunk(range)

          data << "\r\n--#{boundary}\r\n"
          data << "Content-Type: #{blob.content_type_for_serving}\r\n"
          data << "Content-Range: bytes #{range.begin}-#{range.end}/#{blob.byte_size}\r\n\r\n"
          data << chunk
        end

        data << "\r\n--#{boundary}--\r\n"
      end

      response.headers["Accept-Ranges"] = "bytes"
      response.headers["Content-Length"] = data.length.to_s

      send_data(
        data,
        disposition: blob.forced_disposition_for_serving || disposition || DEFAULT_BLOB_STREAMING_DISPOSITION,
        filename: blob.filename.sanitized,
        status: :partial_content,
        type: content_type
      )
    end

    # Stream the blob from storage directly to the response. The disposition can be controlled by setting +disposition+.
    # The content type and filename is set directly from the +blob+.
    def send_blob_stream(blob, disposition: nil) # :doc:
      send_stream(
          filename: blob.filename.sanitized,
          disposition: blob.forced_disposition_for_serving || disposition || DEFAULT_BLOB_STREAMING_DISPOSITION,
          type: blob.content_type_for_serving) do |stream|
        blob.download do |chunk|
          stream.write chunk
        end
      rescue ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
        expires_now
        head :not_found
      rescue
        # Status and caching headers are already set, but not committed.
        # Change the status to 500 manually.
        expires_now
        head :internal_server_error
        raise
      end
    end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "marcel"

# = Active Storage \Variation
#
# A set of transformations that can be applied to a blob to create a variant. This class is exposed via
# the ActiveStorage::Blob#variant method and should rarely be used directly.
#
# In case you do need to use this directly, it's instantiated using a hash of transformations where
# the key is the command and the value is the arguments. Example:
#
#   ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [100, 100], colourspace: "b-w", rotate: "-90", saver: { trim: true })
#
# The options map directly to {ImageProcessing}[https://github.com/janko/image_processing] commands.
class ActiveStorage::Variation
  attr_reader :transformations

  class << self
    # Returns a Variation instance based on the given variator. If the variator is a Variation, it is
    # returned unmodified. If it is a String, it is passed to ActiveStorage::Variation.decode. Otherwise,
    # it is assumed to be a transformations Hash and is passed directly to the constructor.
    def wrap(variator)
      case variator
      when self
        variator
      when String
        decode variator
      else
        new variator
      end
    end

    # Returns a Variation instance with the transformations that were encoded by +encode+.
    def decode(key)
      new ActiveStorage.verifier.verify(key, purpose: :variation)
    end

    # Returns a signed key for the +transformations+, which can be used to refer to a specific
    # variation in a URL or combined key (like <tt>ActiveStorage::Variant#key</tt>).
    def encode(transformations)
      ActiveStorage.verifier.generate(transformations, purpose: :variation)
    end
  end

  def initialize(transformations)
    @transformations = transformations.deep_symbolize_keys
  end

  def default_to(defaults)
    self.class.new transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)
  end

  # Accepts a File object, performs the +transformations+ against it, and
  # saves the transformed image into a temporary file.
  def transform(file, &block)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("transform.active_storage") do
      transformer.transform(file, format: format, &block)
    end
  end

  def format
    transformations.fetch(:format, :png).tap do |format|
      if Marcel::Magic.by_extension(format.to_s).nil?
        raise ArgumentError, "Invalid variant format (#{format.inspect})"
      end
    end
  end

  def content_type
    Marcel::MimeType.for(extension: format.to_s)
  end

  # Returns a signed key for all the +transformations+ that this variation was instantiated with.
  def key
    self.class.encode(transformations)
  end

  def digest
    OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.base64digest Marshal.dump(transformations)
  end

  private
    def transformer
      ActiveStorage.variant_transformer.new(transformations.except(:format))
    end
end

**ActiveStorage & Symbol Serialization: A Deep Dive**

Okay, hold on a second! I need to really think through what's happening here with ActiveStorage and those image variants. It's a bit of a chain of events, and I want to make sure I understand the implications of using symbols, especially for something like `format: :webp`.

First, let's look at the setup. I'm starting with a `Picture` model that has an attached image, and that image has a defined variant: `:large`, with some transformations like resizing and, crucially, a `format: :webp`. The real question is what happens when that variant is created and then later accessed.

My immediate thought is to trace the execution, maybe with `rails runner` or a small reproduction script. Let's start there. I need to understand the flow: `NamedVariant`, `TransformJob`, `CreateVariantsJob`, `Variation.digest`, `VariantWithRecord`, and how `default_to(default_variant_transformations)` or `ActiveJob` serialization handles symbols/strings.

Now, let's dig into the code, starting with `CreateVariantsJob` and `TransformJob`. In `Attachment#create_variants`, I see that the `named_variant.transformations` is `{ resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp }`. That `format: :webp` is a symbol, which is exactly where things get interesting because in `CreateVariantsJob#perform(blob, variants:, process:)`, `variants` contains something like `[{ resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp }]`. This is serialized via ActiveJob! Does this mean the symbol is preserved, or converted to a string? I know ActiveJob serializes hash keys with `_aj_symbol_keys`, but what about symbol values? 

In `ActiveJob` serialization: Does `ActiveJob::Serializers::SymbolSerializer` convert symbol values to strings?

Then, in `Picture#large_image`, `image.variant(:large)` is called, and `transformations` has `format: :webp` (a Symbol)! But in `TransformJob`, it's the blob that's getting the representation with potentially altered transformations, which have been processed through ActiveJob. If that `:webp` became `"webp"` due to ActiveJob serialization, there's a problem.

Here's the problem: The ActiveStorage `Variation.new` class creates a digest which is then used as a cache key: if a different digest is created when the symbol is changed to a string, then the file is not found!

`ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: "webp").digest` would NOT equal `ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp).digest` because `Variation#digest` uses `Marshal.dump(transformations)`. Since that digest is a unique key for the variant, the format mismatch means a different variant (and potentially recreation of the image). That would be bad, very bad.

So, *I need to check this*! I'm not jumping to conclusions; this all hinges on exactly how ActiveJob serializes those symbol values. I need to run a reproduction script to test this hypothesis and verify that the correct transformations are being applied and cached. I should test EVERYTHING too!

messages.thinking:
**The Aha! Moment: A Deep Dive into ActiveStorage Variation Keys**

Okay, BINGO! This is it! Look at this output! It's crystal clear now. I see it: the discrepancy between `v1.key` and `v2.key`, and then `v1.digest` versus `v2.digest`! The root cause is laid bare.

Let me walk through my thought process:

1.  I started with `v1 = ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp)`. Its `digest` is `YMihNeq9GahYwX+32EeyepYXE7Y=`, and the key is a result of the `ActiveStorage.verifier`. But wait a minute! `ActiveStorage.verifier` uses JSON serialization, which means when `v1.key` is encoded in the URL, the `:webp` symbol gets converted to the string `"webp"`. This is the crux of the issue!

2.  On the reader's end, when the book page loads, `image_tag @leaf.picture.large_image` calls `rails_blob_representation_url` with the `variation_key = v1.key`.

3.  The crucial part is how that URL is processed. `Representations::BaseController#set_representation` calls `@blob.representation(params[:variation_key]).processed`. `ActiveStorage::Variation.wrap` then decodes the key using the verifier, which, because of the JSON encoding, returns the hash `{"resize_to_limit" => [1500, 1500], "format" => "webp"}` with `"webp"` (a string)! The `Variation.new` call deep symbolizes that to `{ resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: "webp" }`...but the *format* is still a string. This results in `v2.digest` = `zt77FJ1GTgSdZvhW/wgYp2WAeRQ=`.

4.  Meanwhile, the editor uploaded a photograph, which triggers `CreateVariantsJob`. Because of `ActiveJob`'s `SymbolSerializer`, the `variants:` parameter kept the `:webp` format as a symbol. This means that the associated `TransformJob` created a `VariantRecord` with the correct `variation_digest = "YMihNeq9GahYwX+32EeyepYXE7Y="` (for the symbol `:webp`), and the derived webp file was correctly stored.

5.  So, here's the problem: when the first reader requests the picture, the URL has the `variation_key`, which decodes to the *string* `"webp"`. The system now searches for the `VariantRecord` using the *string* version of the variation digest, the `zt77FJ1GTgSdZvhW/wgYp2WAeRQ=`. This record is *not* found! Because that digest is for the string, not the symbol. Therefore the process *re-runs* the transformation, creates a *second* `VariantRecord` with the *string* version of the digest, and stores a duplicate of the derived webp file.

This is exactly what the problem description describes: duplicate files. I must re-read the problem statement to ensure I have all the details.

> Storage is filling up with duplicate picture files. An editor uploads a photograph, the background job runs and writes the derived copy — then the first reader to open the book triggers the same conversion again, and the second copy is kept next to the first forever.
>
> Make an upload get derived once. After the background work has run, opening the book page and fetching the picture it links to does no image processing, and exactly one derived copy is in storage.
>
> What a reader is served does not change — the same picture they get today, byte for byte.

I need to confirm this is the *only* place the problem occurs, or if it has ripple effects. I'm going to exhaustively check:

1.  Every instance of `has_one_attached`, `has_many_attached`, and `variant` in the codebase.
2.  All tests to see how `Picture` is used and how image processing is tested.
3.  Any code in `lib/rails_ext/` and `config/initializers/extensions.rb` for potential hooks.
4.  And now, the million-dollar question: where to fix it? Do I alter `Picture`, `ActiveStorage`, or both? And are there any other similar configurations in the code that could be affected by

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

This is all critical.

Then, I'll simulate a reader accessing the book page (`get leafable_slug_path(leaf)` or `get book_slug_path(book)`), fetching the picture's URL, and, importantly, what it links to - specifically, where the image is served from (`get <image src>` -> follows redirect to disk service or checks `ActiveStorage::Representations::RedirectController`). This is where I think the problem lies.

Finally, and this is crucial, I need to see if any image processing occurs at this moment (`transform.active_storage` notification!). I'll again check the database post-request: number of `ActiveStorage::VariantRecord` records and the file count in `tmp/storage` to see what changes have been made.

RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails runner '
require "active_support/testing/time_helpers"
include ActiveJob::TestHelper

storage_root = ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root
FileUtils.rm_rf(storage_root)
FileUtils.mkdir_p(storage_root)

transforms = []
ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") do |*args|
  transforms << args
end

book = Book.first
leaf = nil

puts "--- Step 1: Upload picture & run background jobs ---"
perform_enqueued_jobs do
  picture = Picture.new(caption: "Test photo")
  picture.image.attach(
    io: File.open(Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/white-rabbit.webp")),
    filename: "white-rabbit.webp",
    content_type: "image/webp"
  )
  leaf = book.press(picture, title: "Photo")
end

blob = leaf.picture.image.blob
puts "Transforms during upload+jobs: #{transforms.size}"
puts "Variant records after upload+jobs: #{blob.variant_records.count} (#{blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest)})"
files_after_upload = Dir.glob("#{storage_root}/**/*").select { |f| File.file?(f) }
puts "Files in storage after upload+jobs: #{files_after_upload.size}"
files_after_upload.each { |f| puts "  #{f}" }

puts "--- Step 2: Reader opens book page & fetches image ---"
transforms.clear
session = ActionDispatch::Integration::Session.new(Rails.application)
session.get "/#{book.id}/#{book.slug}/#{leaf.id}/#{leaf.slug}"
puts "Page response: #{session.response.status}"

# Extract image src from HTML
img_src = session.response.body[/<img[^>]+src="([^"]+)"/, 1]
puts "Image src: #{img_src}"

session.get img_src
puts "Image representation response: #{session.response.status} -> #{session.response.location}"

puts "Transforms during reader request: #{transforms.size}"
puts "Variant records after reader request: #{blob.variant_records.reload.count} (#{blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest)})"
files_after_reader = Dir.glob("#{storage_root}/**/*").select { |f| File.file?(f) }
puts "Files in storage after reader request: #{files_after_reader.size}"
files_after_reader.each { |f| puts "  #{f}" }
'

**ActiveStorage Variation Debugging - A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm looking at this ActiveStorage implementation, and boom! It's reproducing an image transformation *exactly*. I see the initial upload process: image upload, background jobs running, and the variants and files stored. Now, a reader fetches the image, and a new variant is created and stored.

Wait a minute, two *different* `variation_digest` values? That's not right. I need to dig into the `transformations` hashes for *both* those digests. Okay, let's compare those transformation hashes, focusing on the differences. Is it the `:format => :webp` vs. `format: "webp"` or maybe the order of the keys? I'm seeing `{:resize_to_limit => ..., :format => ...}` versus `{:format => ..., :resize_to_limit => ...}`.

Hold on, I see the `variation_key` in the URL. It's `{"resize_to_limit":[1500,1500],"format":"webp"}` compared to `{"format":"webp","resize_to_limit":[1500,1500]}`. And look at the base64 encoded part of that URL – I can decode it. It seems like the JSON keys for the format are first: `"data":{"format":"webp","resize_to_limit":[1500,1500]}`. Why is "format" first?

Let's look at the `Blob::Representable#variant` method. It calls `Variation.wrap(transformations).default_to(default_variant_transformations)`. The `default_variant_transformations` is defined as `{ format: "webp" }`.

So, it's `transformations.reverse_merge({ format: "webp" })`. In Ruby, that's equivalent to `{ format: "webp" }.merge(transformations)`. So, `{ format: "webp" }` is the first key in the hash, and the merge overwrites it. This means the order is being preserved! And when I dump a hash with `Marshal.dump`, the order *is* preserved, with `:format` being first in the key order, which is used for the digest.

Now, let's compare the processes: During the `TransformJob`, the `blob.representation(transformations)` call goes through `blob.variant(transformations)`. This results in `{ format: :webp, resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500] }`, and the `:format` is a Symbol! However, the `Representations::RedirectController` goes through the same logic: The URL key gets decoded, and it's `{ format: "webp", resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500] }` where `"webp"` is a String.

Hold up! Let's cover all the edge cases. What if the `format: "webp"` (string) is used in `Picture` instead of the symbol? What if format is not `:webp` vs `"webp"`? What if there are other nuances in `Variation`, `default_to`, or `Picture`? I need to use `rails runner` to test all of this.

+module ActiveStorage::Sluggable
+  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
+
+  included do
+    before_create :set_slug
+  end
+
+  def slug_path
+    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.action_text_markdown_upload_path(slug)
+  end
+
+  private
+    def set_slug
+      self.slug = "#{slug_basename}-#{SecureRandom.alphanumeric(6)}.#{slug_extension}"
+    end
+
+    def slug_basename
+      File.basename(slug_filename, ".*").parameterize
+    end
+
+    def slug_extension
+      File.extname(slug_filename).delete(".").parameterize
+    end
+
+    def slug_filename
+      slug.presence || filename.to_s
+    end
+end
+

+  ActiveStorage::Attachment.include ActiveStorage::Sluggable

**Deep Dive into ActiveStorage Variation and Potential Optimization**

Okay, let's break this down. My goal here is to understand the nuances of ActiveStorage variations, identify the root cause of the duplicate image generation problem, and ensure that the solution adheres to the critical requirement: serving the *exact* same byte-for-byte image to readers after the initial processing. I'm going to carefully analyze the transformation process in Rails to see where this is happening.

First, I examined `ActiveStorage::Variation`. I see how it's initialized with transformations, how it handles defaults via `default_to`, formats, content types, and crucially, how it generates the key and digest. The `key` uses `ActiveStorage.verifier` with JSON encoding, while the `digest` uses `Marshal.dump`. This is a *major* point of concern, as I know that JSON and `Marshal` handle symbols differently, and this could be part of the problem. Specifically, JSON converts symbols to strings during serialization.

Next, I looked at a concrete example in `app/models/picture.rb` with a declared variant `large`, noting the `resize_to_limit`, `format: :webp`, and `process: :later` settings. I then examined what happens in TWO key places: background job processing and view rendering.

In the background job, specifically within `CreateVariantsJob` and `TransformJob`, I see the `transformations` hash gets passed around (via ActiveJob preserving symbols). It is the `default_to` and `reverse_merge` operations that seem relevant here. The final transformations end up being SHA1 digested with `Marshal.dump`.

In the view rendering, I followed the path from `image_tag` to `url_for(variant)` to `variation.key`, which uses `ActiveStorage.verifier.generate`. This is where the JSON serialization and deserialization occurs. When encoded, the transformations are JSON serialized, and when fetched by a reader and then decoded, it's JSON deserialized. The important thing I saw is that when encoded and decoded in this way, symbols are stringified, resulting in a *different* hash than the one created with `Marshal.dump` (in the background job). This difference in digest calculation is the core of the problem!

I then considered what happens when the reader fetches the image from the redirected URL, the `Representations::BaseController`. Here, the `params[:variation_key]` is decoded, deep symbolized, and then *used*! The crucial detail here is that the decoded hash has string keys, whereas the digest in the background job used symbol keys.

I'm now thinking: if the digest calculation is different, ActiveStorage will reprocess the image, leading to duplicates. It’s imperative to have consistency.

Now, I'm analyzing the cases: What if the image's original format is not WebP? What if `"webp"` is used vs `:webp`? What if `Picture#large_image` or `ActiveStorage::Variation` is changed? I went through what happens with `.jpg`, `.png`, `.webp`, `.tiff`. The analysis is clear: When the key generation uses `"webp"` (String) in all stages and the background job, the digests *are* the same. And I'm seeing that regardless of the initial image format, `format: "webp"` ends up resolving to `format: "webp"`.

I'm starting to think: *Is `format: "webp"` in `Picture` enough?* What if `format` is `:webp` or if no `format` is passed? Or, if someone does not pass `format:`, the defaults kick in...

And now, I'm thinking, "Does this affect anything else?" I checked various views and controllers using pictures, including the ones that render picture URLs and the `image_tag` in multiple views. The behavior is consistent: the browser is getting the URL for the processed variant.

I checked what happens with `image_processing` / `vips`, and I see the exact same bytes are produced, whether the symbol or string is used. Then I got to the problem! `Variation#key` uses `ActiveStorage.verifier.generate`, *with* JSON encoding (with its stringification of symbols), whereas `Variation#digest` uses `Marshal.dump` which keeps the symbols as symbols. And I see that the filename is the same, so there is no impact.

Finally, I'm considering: Is there a fundamental Rails/ActiveStorage bug with `Variation`, or the JSON symbol handling and how it's used? Is this a problem because of how `Picture` is declaring `format: :webp`?

**Analyzing the ActiveStorage Variant Mismatch Issue**

Okay, so the issue at hand is the duplication of derived picture files in storage. It seems like the core problem revolves around discrepancies in how the `ActiveStorage::Variation` digest is generated and how it is later decoded, especially concerning the `format` option (symbols vs. strings).

My initial instinct was to examine the code where variants are defined, specifically within the `Picture` model and its `image` attachment. I needed to confirm the exact variant definition: `format: :webp`. A quick grep confirmed this across the application. Also `Book` and `ActionText::Markdown` don't need work. The prompt also states that the issue is when a reader triggers the image conversion, meaning the reader is triggering the problem, so a reader is hitting `@leaf.picture.large_image` (or `leaf.leafable.large_image`) and it's calling `image.variant(:large)`.

The crucial detail is that the background job, using `format: :webp`, produces a digest. However, the reader, potentially using `format: "webp"`, generates a *different* digest, leading to the same image being processed again and again.

So, I need to look into how `ActiveStorage.verifier` serializes the `transformations` hash, which is what is used by `ActiveStorage::Variation`'s `key` method. It seems that `ActiveStorage.verifier` uses JSON, which converts symbols to strings (e.g., `:webp` becomes `"webp"`). But, the `digest` is created using `Marshal.dump` and has `transformations`, which *preserves* the symbol. This difference is what's causing the mismatch!

I've got three options:
1.  Simply fix `app/models/picture.rb` with a string.
2.  Fix `ActiveStorage::Variation` in `lib/rails_ext/` by modifying how the `digest` is generated.
3.  Do BOTH!

The solution would be to make the `digest` convert all symbols to strings during its computation, and also make the variant option use strings.

Let's carefully consider. If I only change `app/models/picture.rb` to `format: "webp"`, that fixes the most immediate problem, but it doesn't address the underlying inconsistency. What if someone later uses a symbol somewhere else, or uses the `image.variant` method directly? Also, why is there a string? If I change `ActiveStorage::Variation`, I can fix this root cause!

So, the preferred fix would be to modify the `digest` method to use `Marshal.dump(transformations.deep_transform_values { |value| value.is_a?(Symbol) ? value.to_s : value })` to consistently generate the digest. This ensures that the digest matches what's stored (and what's decoded). I'll also modify the model definition to also use strings.

After the change, existing records won't be broken because their `2iK...` `VariantRecord` will match their previous digest.

Finally, I checked the autoloading of the class, making sure my patch will work with or without changes to the autoloading order.

I will implement the fix in `lib/rails_ext/` with `ActiveStorage::Variation` and ensure the change is consistent. I'll test with different image types (JPEG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, TIFF) to ensure the solution is robust.

**The Optimal Solution for ActiveStorage Variant Formatting**

Okay, it's clear. We have a discrepancy in how Rails handles variant formats, specifically with the use of symbols versus strings (`:webp` vs `"webp"`), and it's causing issues. My goal is a fix that's robust, future-proof, and doesn't introduce any regressions.

The initial thought was to simply change the format within `Picture` to `"webp"`, but that's a narrow fix. It won't address the underlying problem and leaves us vulnerable to similar issues cropping up in other parts of the codebase. It also doesn't consider direct calls to the image variant.

The more comprehensive solution is to patch `ActiveStorage::Variation` in `lib/rails_ext/`. This seems safe because the extensions directory is specifically designed for this purpose, and the extensions are loaded early in the Rails boot process.

The key is in the `digest` method of `ActiveStorage::Variation`. Currently, it uses `Marshal.dump` which is sensitive to symbols vs strings. If we modify `digest` to normalize symbol values to strings using `deep_transform_values`, we can ensure that any variant with the same transformations, regardless of whether it uses symbols or strings, will generate the same digest.

The benefit of this approach is that it is a *universal* fix. It corrects this behavior for any variants (not just images) and prevents duplicates when decoding URL parameters and generating variants for `TransformJob`. Further, by applying the fix at the `ActiveStorage::Variation` level, any future variants will automatically be consistent.

However, we need to test this thoroughly! We need to make sure that the `deep_transform_values` method handles all data types correctly to avoid unexpected behavior. We also have to check that the patch is compatible with existing production data. Since `ActiveStorage::Variation`'s `digest` method is used in tracked variants, the patch must ensure the same digest is generated.

By implementing this fix at the source (`ActiveStorage::Variation`), we create a robust, consistent, and forward-compatible solution.

require "active_job"
ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :test

storage_root = ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root

transforms = []

  transforms << args
end

book = Book.first
book.update!(published: true, everyone_access: true)

[
  ["white-rabbit.webp", Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/white-rabbit.webp"), "image/webp"],
  ["writebook-manual.jpg", Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg"), "image/jpeg"],

].each do |filename, path, content_type|
  puts "=== Testing #{filename} (#{content_type}) ==="
  FileUtils.rm_rf(storage_root)
  FileUtils.mkdir_p(storage_root)
  transforms.clear

  ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.perform_enqueued_jobs = true
  ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.perform_enqueued_at_jobs = true
  picture = Picture.new(caption: "Test photo")
  picture.image.attach(io: File.open(path), filename: filename, content_type: content_type)
  leaf = book.press(picture, title: "Photo #{filename}")
  ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.perform_enqueued_jobs = false

  blob = leaf.picture.image.blob
  puts "  Transforms during upload+jobs: #{transforms.size}"
  puts "  Variant records after upload+jobs: #{blob.variant_records.count} (#{blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest)})"
  files_after_upload = Dir.glob("#{storage_root}/**/*").select { |f| File.file?(f) }
  puts "  Files in storage after upload+jobs: #{files_after_upload.size}"

  transforms.clear
  session = ActionDispatch::Integration::Session.new(Rails.application)

  # Open book TOC page
  session.get "/#{book.id}/#{book.slug}"
  raise "Book page failed: #{session.response.status}" unless session.response.status == 200

  # Open picture leaf page
  session.get "/#{book.id}/#{book.slug}/#{leaf.id}/#{leaf.slug}"
  raise "Leaf page failed: #{session.response.status}" unless session.response.status == 200

  img_src = session.response.body[/<figure[^>]*>.*?<img[^>]+src="([^"]+)"/m, 1]
  session.get img_src
  raise "Representation failed: #{session.response.status}" unless session.response.status == 302

  redirect_url = session.response.location
  session.get redirect_url
  raise "Disk fetch failed: #{session.response.status}" unless session.response.status == 200

  served_bytes = session.response.body

  expected_bytes = ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp).transform(File.open(path), &:read)

  puts "  Transforms during reader request: #{transforms.size}"

  files_after_reader = Dir.glob("#{storage_root}/**/*").select { |f| File.file?(f) }
  puts "  Files in storage after reader request: #{files_after_reader.size}"
  puts "  Byte-for-byte identical? #{served_bytes == expected_bytes} (#{served_bytes.bytesize} bytes)"

  leaf.destroy!
  blob.purge
end

ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(subscriber)
FileUtils.rm_rf(storage_root)
'

    assert_response :no_content

    updated_picture = Picture.last
    assert_equal "New picture", updated_picture.title
    assert_equal "white-rabbit.webp", updated_picture.image.filename.to_s
  end

  test "update caption" do
    get edit_leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture))
    assert_response :ok

    put leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture)), params: {
      picture: {
        caption: "New caption"
      } }

    assert_response :no_content

    updated_picture = Picture.last

    assert_equal "New caption", updated_picture.caption
    assert_equal "reading.webp", updated_picture.image.filename.to_s
  end

  test "uploaded picture is derived once and reused when a reader fetches it" do
    transforms = 0
    subscriber = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") { transforms += 1 }

    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      post book_pictures_path(books(:handbook), format: :turbo_stream), params: {
        leaf: { title: "White Rabbit" },
        picture: { image: fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp") }
      }
    end

    assert_response :success
    assert_equal 1, transforms

    leaf = books(:handbook).leaves.order(:id).last
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob

    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.count
    derived_blob = blob.variant_records.first.image.blob
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(derived_blob.key)

    books(:handbook).update!(published: true)
    sign_in :jz

    transforms = 0

    assert_no_difference -> { ActiveStorage::Blob.count } do
      assert_no_difference -> { ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.count } do
        get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
        assert_response :success

        get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
        assert_response :success

        img_src = css_select("figure.page--picture img").first["src"]
        get img_src
        assert_response :redirect

        get response.location
        assert_response :success
      end
    end

    assert_equal 0, transforms

    expected_bytes = ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ], format: :webp)
      .transform(file_fixture("white-rabbit.webp").open, &:read)
    assert_equal expected_bytes, response.body
  ensure
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(subscriber) if subscriber
  end
end
